note: Hand-labelled sample for docshelf-build classify (2026-11-22), in three splits. Pages from the 0.2.0 trial's llms.txt docvols: langchain = docs.langchain.com build/python.txt, opencode = opencode.ai llms.txt. split 'calibration' (124 pages): picked as a spread over each sorted key list (the langchain plan has a single section, "Python", so its spread is by key prefix) (every third langchain page, every other opencode page with signals); rules-1 was tuned on these only (then checked on holdout, then on unseen data); rules-2 on calibration + holdout. split 'holdout' (84 pages, added 2026-11-22 and labelled by a different reader; not used for rules-1 tuning, but rules-2 was tuned on calibration + holdout): every remaining opencode page with signals, and every fourth of the remaining langchain pages with signals (sorted keys, starting from the second). split 'fresh' (62 pages, added 2026-11-22 and labelled by a reader who never saw the rules' thresholds; the only data rules-2 never saw, so the one clean out-of-sample measure): langchain-ts = docs.langchain.com TypeScript sub-index (oss/javascript and langsmith/javascript pages), 62 pages spread evenly over its 236 sorted keys with signals. label 'reference': an agent looks things up in it (API pages, parameters, options, config keys, error lists, CLI flags, integration pages that are mostly signatures and settings). label 'guide': tutorials, concepts, overviews, how-tos told in steps, marketing, legal, status, changelogs and release notes. A page that is both goes by what most of it is. Labels were read from each cached page, not from the signals; signals are copied from the plan. Pages are sorted by site, then split, then key. No page text.
